newsitem.title: POLAND: Clinton nominates Ferguson, Gramlich to Fed board.
newsitem.headline: Clinton nominates Ferguson, Gramlich to Fed board.

text.p: President Clinton said on Thursday he would nominate Edward Gramlich and Roger Ferguson to the board of directors of the Federal Reserve system.
Clinton's formal announcement of the long-awaited nominations came in Poland, where he was helping to celebrate the prospective entry of central europe's largest state into the NATO alliance.

Gramlich is an economics professor and Dean of the School of Public Policy at the University of Michigan. Ferguson has been a partner at the New York-based international consultancy firm McKinsey and Co, Inc since 1991.
The two nominees, who must be confirmed by the Senate, will bring to full strength the seven-member Federal Reserve Board.

Two vacancies on the central bank's board opened up this year with the departure of Janet Yellen for the White House Council of Economic Advisers and Lawrence Lindsey for the conservative Amercian Enterprise Institute think tank.
The Board's primary function is the formulation of monetary policy. It also has broad supervisory and regulatory responsibility over the activities of banks and other financial institutions.
